examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Sum or Difference of Three or More Matrices Using Distributivity
examples.worked_solution:
First, we simplify the expression by distributing the subtraction over the matrices in the parentheses: 

$$
\begin{aligned}A+C-(B+A) & =A+C-B-A \\  & =\cancel{A}+C-B-\cancel{A} \\  & =C-B\end{aligned}
$$

We are left with a single subtraction. So, we subtract the corresponding entries of the two matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}C-B & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ -6 & 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3-3 & -1-(-1) \\ 1-2 & 2-0 \\ -6-(-4) & 1-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Performing the operations on each corresponding entry, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}R+S+T & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -3 \\ -4 & 2 \\ -1 & -5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}7 & -5 \\ 12 & -8 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3+7+3 & -3+(-5)+0 \\ -4+12+0 & 2+(-8)+7 \\ -1+5+0 & -5+(-3)+2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -8 \\ 8 & 1 \\ 4 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
